title: Attributional Safety Failures in Large Language Models under Code-Mixed Perturbations
base_benchmarks: Culturally grounded dataset introduced by Banerjee et al. (2025)
findings: Large Language Models that are safely aligned in English exhibit catastrophic safety failures when prompted with code-mixed inputs, especially in culturally sensitive contexts including religion. For instance, prompts about religious marginalization trigger significantly more harmful responses when code-mixed. The study's 'saliency drift attribution' analysis reveals that models lose focus on safety-critical tokens (including religious terms) in code-mixed prompts, effectively blinding them to the harmful intent and causing them to bypass their safety guardrails.
references: Abubakar Abid et al. 2021. Persistent anti-Muslim bias in large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2101.05783 (2021).

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the generation of harmful content in response to culturally sensitive prompts, including those related to religious themes, stereotypes, and marginalization. The primary goal is to assess how code-mixing (blending languages) affects the safety alignment of Large Language Models in these contexts.
